SEARCH
Package gov.cdc.izgateway.soap.fault

Interface FaultSupport

All Known Implementing Classes:
DestinationConnectionFault, Fault, HubClientFault, MessageSupport, MessageTooLargeFault, SecurityFault, UnexpectedExceptionFault, UnknownDestinationFault, UnsupportedOperationFault
public interface FaultSupport
Access to this interface is supported by Faults created in this package to enable structured diagnostics and logging with Faults.

  • Method Details

    • getSummary

      String getSummary()
      The summary of the fault, used in logging to classify errors. This should be a short (invalid input: '<' 20 characters) descriptive summary of the fault. Each fault should support just a few summary values and they should be determined by the constructor rather than user provided string values.
      Returns:
      A summary of what went wrong.

    • getDetail

      String getDetail()
      The details associated with what went wrong. This allows users to providee variation in fault details, such as parameter causing the problem, or a more detailed description of the error.
      Returns:
      The details associated with the fault.

    • getMessage

      String getMessage()
      The error message associated with the fault. By convention, this is constructed in the form Summary: Detail
      Returns:
      The error message.

    • getDiagnostics

      String getDiagnostics()
      A human readable explanation of how to address the fault or what it means. Explain in words that would be meaningful to an end user.
      Returns:
      The diagnostics associated with this fault.

    • getCode

      String getCode()
      The unique error code associated with this message. This is a short numeric code suiteable for automated interpretation that embodies the type of fault, the subtype and the retry strategy to apply. It is a 3 digit code in which the first digit indicate the fault type, the second provides the subtype, and the third, the retry strategy.
      Returns:
      The code for error

    • getRetry

      RetryStrategy getRetry()
      The retry strategy that should be applied by application software before retrying the communiication.
      Returns:
      The retry strategy.

    • getFaultName

      String getFaultName()
      The name of the fault to report in logging.
      Returns:
      The fault type
